nodes.summary: Suppose `X = W * H`, where `W` has a pure row for every factor (`IsSeparable Wᵀ`: for each `a` a row `i` with `W i · = e • e_a`, `e > 0`) and `H` has a pure column for every factor (`IsSeparable H`). Then every factorization `X = W' * H'` with `W', H' ≥ 0` and the same inner dimension agrees with `(W, H)` up to a permutation `σ` and positive scalings `d` of the factors: `W' · a = d a • W · (σ a)` and…
nodes.title: Essential uniqueness of NMF when both factors are separable

nodes.summary: For every real matrix `X` and every finite inner index type `k`, the objective attains its infimum over pairs `W, H ≥ 0` (entrywise).
nodes.title: Existence of a minimizer

nodes.summary: A nonnegative matrix has a nonnegative factorization of inner dimension `nonnegRank X`.
nodes.title: Existence of a factorization of nonnegative-rank inner dimension

nodes.summary: If `G * K = 1` with `G` and `K` entrywise nonnegative, then there are a permutation `σ` and positive weights `d` with `G a b = d b` if `a = σ b` and `0` otherwise.
nodes.title: A nonnegative matrix with a nonnegative inverse is monomial

nodes.summary: The gradient of the objective with respect to `H`: `2 (Wᵀ W H - Wᵀ X)`.
nodes.title: Gradient of the NMF objective with respect to H

nodes.summary: The gradient of the objective with respect to `W`: `2 (W H Hᵀ - X Hᵀ)`.
nodes.title: Gradient of the NMF objective with respect to W

nodes.summary: `gradH X W H a j` is the partial derivative of the objective in the entry `H a j`.
nodes.title: Partial derivative of the NMF objective in an entry of H

nodes.summary: `gradW X W H i a` is the partial derivative of the objective in the entry `W i a`.
nodes.title: Partial derivative of the NMF objective in an entry of W

nodes.summary: A fixed point of the Lee–Seung sweep with all entries of `W` and `H` positive has both gradients zero, so it satisfies the KKT conditions.
nodes.title: Positive fixed points are KKT points

nodes.summary: The Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions of `min ‖X - W H‖_F²` subject to `W, H ≥ 0`: primal feasibility, dual feasibility (nonnegative gradients) and complementary slackness.
nodes.title: Karush–Kuhn–Tucker point of nonnegative matrix factorization

nodes.summary: `H` is separable: every factor `a` has a pure column, a column `j` of `H` equal to a positive multiple of the unit vector `e_a`. For `X = W * H` this makes column `j` of `X` a positive multiple of column `a` of `W` (a sample containing only factor `a`). Applied to `Wᵀ` it says that every factor has a pure row of `W` (an "anchor" feature of factor `a` alone).
nodes.title: Separable factor matrix

nodes.summary: Write the bulk matrix (genes × samples) as `C * P`, the cell-type profiles `C` times the cell-type proportions `P`. If the proportions of sample `j` are nonnegative and sum to `1` and every cell type expresses gene `g` at a level in `[lo, hi]`, then the bulk level of `g` in sample `j` lies in `[lo, hi]`.
nodes.title: Gene-expression deconvolution

nodes.summary: If `updateH X W H = H`, then `H a j * gradH X W H a j = 0` for every entry.
nodes.title: Complementary slackness at a fixed point of the `H` update

nodes.summary: Complementary slackness at a fixed point of the `W` update.
nodes.title: Complementary slackness at a fixed point of the `W` update

nodes.summary: The nonnegative rank of a nonnegative matrix is at most its number of columns.
nodes.title: Nonnegative rank is at most the number of columns

nodes.summary: A nonnegative factorization with inner dimension `r` bounds the nonnegative rank by `r`.
nodes.title: A nonnegative factorization bounds the nonnegative rank

nodes.summary: The nonnegative rank of `X`: the least `r` such that `X = W * H` with `W : m × r` and `H : r × n` entrywise nonnegative (Cohen and Rothblum 1993). If `X` has a negative entry no such factorization exists and the value is the junk value `sInf ∅ = 0`.
nodes.title: Nonnegative rank of a matrix

nodes.summary: The objective is nonnegative.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the NMF objective

nodes.summary: The objective is non-increasing along the Lee–Seung iterates started from `W, H ≥ 0`, for `X ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: The objective is non-increasing along the Lee–Seung iterates

nodes.summary: One Lee–Seung sweep does not increase the objective, for `X, W, H ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: One Lee–Seung sweep does not increase the objective

nodes.summary: Transposing exchanges the roles of `W` and `H`: `‖Xᵀ - Hᵀ Wᵀ‖² = ‖X - W H‖²`.
nodes.title: The NMF objective is invariant under transposition

nodes.summary: Lee–Seung, `H` step (Lee and Seung 2001, Theorem 1): for `W, H ≥ 0`, the multiplicative update of `H` does not increase `‖X - W H‖_F²`. The proof is the auxiliary-function argument: the quadratic term of the exact expansion is bounded by Lee and Seung's diagonal majorant (here through a weighted Cauchy–Schwarz inequality), and the update minimizes the majorant. `X` may have any sign.
nodes.title: Lee–Seung, `H` step

nodes.summary: For `W, H ≥ 0`, the multiplicative update of `W` does not increase `‖X - W H‖_F²`.
nodes.title: Lee–Seung, `W` step

nodes.summary: The NMF objective: the squared Frobenius distance `‖X - W H‖_F² = ∑ i j, (X i j - (W H) i j)²` between the data `X` and the product `W * H`.
nodes.title: Objective of nonnegative matrix factorization

nodes.summary: The nonnegative rank of a nonnegative matrix is at least its rank.
nodes.title: The nonnegative rank of a nonnegative matrix is at least its rank

nodes.summary: Mutational signatures (Alexandrov et al. 2013). Write the mutation-count matrix (mutation types × samples) as `W * H`, signatures (columns of `W`) times exposures `H`. If every signature is a probability vector over mutation types, the total mutation count of sample `j` equals the sum of its exposures.
nodes.title: Mutational signatures

nodes.summary: Column sums of a product: `∑ i, (W H) i j = ∑ a, (∑ i, W i a) H a j`.
nodes.title: Column sums of a matrix product

nodes.summary: One sweep keeps both factors nonnegative when `X ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: A Lee–Seung sweep preserves nonnegativity

nodes.summary: One sweep of the Lee–Seung algorithm: update `H`, then update `W` using the new `H`.
nodes.title: One sweep of the Lee–Seung algorithm

nodes.summary: The `H` update keeps `H` nonnegative when `X`, `W`, `H` are nonnegative.
nodes.title: The Lee–Seung H update preserves nonnegativity

nodes.summary: The Lee–Seung multiplicative update of `H` (Lee and Seung 2001, Theorem 1): `H a j ← H a j * (Wᵀ X) a j / (Wᵀ W H) a j`. An entry with a zero denominator becomes `0` (Lean's `x / 0 = 0`).
nodes.title: Lee–Seung multiplicative update of H

nodes.summary: The `W` update is the `H` update of the transposed problem.
nodes.title: The W update is the H update of the transposed problem

nodes.summary: The `W` update keeps `W` nonnegative when `X`, `W`, `H` are nonnegative.
nodes.title: The Lee–Seung W update preserves nonnegativity

nodes.summary: The Lee–Seung multiplicative update of `W` (Lee and Seung 2001, Theorem 1): `W i a ← W i a * (X Hᵀ) i a / (W H Hᵀ) i a`. An entry with a zero denominator becomes `0`.
nodes.title: Lee–Seung multiplicative update of W

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
